```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(fs)
library(cbsodataR)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(tidyterra)
library(terra)
library(maptiles)
library(patchwork)

epsg_wgs_84 <- 4326   # WGS 84
epsg_web_merc <- 3857 # Web Mercator
epsg_nl <- 28992      # Amersfoort / RD New
```

```{r}
#| label: import-data
#| cache: true
#| output: false

lisa <- read_sf("data/lisa2017.parquet") # internal

gwl  <- read_sf("data/GWL.gpkg") |> # internal
  remove_empty(which = c("rows", "cols")) |>
  remove_constant() |>
  mutate(oid = row_number(), .before = everything())

# from https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/dossier/nederland-regionaal/geografische-data/gegevens-per-postcode
bevolking_pc6 <- read_sf("data/cbs_pc6_2025_v1.gpkg") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) replace_values(x, c(-99997, -99995) ~ NA))) |>
  remove_empty("cols")

# from https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/dossier/nederland-regionaal/geografische-data/kaart-van-500-meter-bij-500-meter-met-statistieken
cbs500m <- read_sf("data/cbs_vk500_2025_v1.gpkg") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) replace_values(x, c(-99997, -99995) ~ NA))) |>
  remove_empty("cols")

stedelijkheid <- cbs_get_data("86247NED") |>
  select(
    gemeente_code = Code_1,
    gemeente = Naam_2,
    stedelijkheid_code = Code_54,
    stedelijkheid = Omschrijving_55,
    inwoners = Inwonertal_56,
    omgevingsadressendichtheid = Omgevingsadressendichtheid_57
  ) |>
  mutate(
    gemeente = str_trim(gemeente),
    stedelijkheid = fct_reorder(stedelijkheid, stedelijkheid_code),
    .keep = "unused"
  )

# internal 2018 Public Transport Accessibility Level (PTAL) dataset
ptal <- read_sf("data/ptal2018.gpkg") |>
  mutate(ptal = fct_rev(factor(ptal)))

nl_border <- read_sf("data/landsgrens.geojson") # internal, 2023

# GWL 10 and 20 km diameter circles
circles <- read_sf("data/cirkels.gpkg")
circles_8 <- read_sf("data/cirkels_8km.gpkg")

# Basemap layers ---------------------------------------------------------------

bebouwd_gebied <- read_sf(path("data", "processed", "bebouwd_gebied.gpkg"))
natura2000_nl <- read_sf(path("data", "processed", "natura2000_nl.gpkg"))
tent_trein <- read_sf(path("data", "processed", "tent_trein_nl_be_de.gpkg"))
tent_weg <- read_sf(path("data", "processed", "tent_weg_nl_be_de.gpkg"))
tent_water <- read_sf(path("data", "processed", "tent_water_nl_be_de.gpkg"))
```

## Introduction

The Netherlands is planning to address the housing crisis
by building new housing, with concentrations in several large-scale locations.
These grootschalige woningbouwlocaties must have access to jobs and amenities
by sustainable modes of transport—public transport, bicycle, and foot—
to ensure that they are both sustainable and livable.

## Public Transport

What about public transport?
Are the large-scale housing locations accessible by train, bus, tram, and metro?
Does the accessibility level vary within the housing area?
Let's take a look using the public transport accesibility level (PTAL) metric.

### PTAL

```{r}
#| label: ptal-leaflet

gwl_wgs84 <- gwl |>
  st_transform(4326)

ptal_cbs_500m <- cbs500m |>
  left_join(ptal |> st_drop_geometry(), by = c("crs28992res500m" = "cbs_cell_i")) |>
  mutate(ptal = ptal |> replace_values(NA ~ "1a"))

gwl_cbs_stedelijkheid <- gwl |>
  left_join(
    stedelijkheid,
    by = c("Gemeente" = "gemeente"),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )

ptal_gwl <- ptal_cbs_500m |>
  st_join(
    gwl_cbs_stedelijkheid |> select(-id),
    left = FALSE,
    suffix = c("", "_gemeente"),
  )

ptal_gwl_wgs84 <- ptal_gwl |>
  st_transform(epsg_wgs_84)

ptal_levels <- levels(ptal$ptal)

ptal_pal <- colorFactor(
  reverse = TRUE,
  palette = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(length(ptal_levels), "YlGnBu"),
  levels = ptal_levels
)

leaflet() |>
  # addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addTiles(
    urlTemplate = paste0(
      "https://service.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-achtergrondkaart/",
      "wmts/v2_0/grijs/EPSG:3857/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
    ),
    attribution = paste(
      'Kaartgegevens: <a href="https://www.kadaster.nl/">',
      'Kadaster</a> / PDOK'
    )
  ) |>
  addPolygons(
    data = ptal_gwl_wgs84,
    color = ~ ptal_pal(ptal),
    fillColor = ~ ptal_pal(ptal),
    opacity = 0.7,
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    weight = 1,
    popup = ~ paste0(
      "<strong>", GWL, "</strong>", ": ", Subproject, "<br>",
      "CBS stedelijkheid (gemeente): ", stedelijkheid_gemeente, "<br>",
      "Woningen subproject: ", Subcapacit, "<br>",
      "Woningen project: ", Projcapaci, "<br>",
      "Woningen ", GWL, " 2030: ", TOT2030, "<br>",
      "Woningen ", GWL, " 2040: ", TOT2040, "<br>"
    )
  ) |>
  addPolygons(
    data = gwl_wgs84,
    fill = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 0.5
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = ptal_pal(ptal_levels),
    labels = ptal_levels,
    title = "PTAL"
  ) |>
  addScaleBar(
    position = "bottomleft",
    options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ptal-small-multiples
#| fig-cap: "OV-bereikbaarheid (PTAL) van grootschalige woningbouwlocaties"
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 10

# 1. Get Kadaster BRT basemap tiles from PDOK ----------------------------------
brt <- create_provider(
  name = "PDOK BRT-A",
  url = paste0(
    "https://service.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-achtergrondkaart/",
    "wmts/v2_0/grijs/EPSG:3857/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
  ),
  citation = "Kaartgegevens © Kadaster (CC BY 4.0)"
)

brt_tiles <- get_tiles(
  x = circles_8,
  provider = brt,
  zoom = 10,
  project = FALSE,
  cachedir = "data/raw/brt_z10"
)

# 2. Function make_map to plot each small multiple map -------------------------

make_map <- function(zoom_area) {
  zoom_area_merc <- zoom_area |>
    st_transform(crs = epsg_web_merc) |>
    st_set_agr("constant")
  
  bbox <- st_bbox(zoom_area_merc)
  
  tiles_crop <- crop(
    brt_tiles,
    ext(
      bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"],
      bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"]
    )
  )
  
  # crop to circles
  tiles_masked <- mask(tiles_crop,mask = vect(zoom_area_merc))
  
  ptal_gwl_crop <- ptal_gwl |>
    st_transform(crs = epsg_web_merc) |>
    st_set_agr("constant") |>
    st_intersection(zoom_area_merc)

  gwl_crop <- gwl |>
    st_transform(crs = epsg_web_merc) |>
    st_set_agr("constant") |>
    st_intersection(zoom_area_merc)

  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster_rgb(data = tiles_masked) +
    geom_sf(
      data = ptal_gwl_crop,
      aes(fill = ptal),
      alpha = 0.7,
      show.legend = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_sf(
      data = gwl_crop,
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_brewer(
      name = "PTAL",
      palette = "YlGnBu",
      direction = -1,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    coord_sf(
      xlim = bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")],
      ylim = bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")],
      crs = epsg_web_merc
    ) +
    labs(title = zoom_area$naam) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16))
}

# 3. Make all maps, facet them with patchwork, save, and plot ------------------

maps <- circles_8 |>
  split(seq_len(nrow(circles_8))) |> # need to split because of sf weirdness
  map(make_map)

p <- wrap_plots(
  maps,
  ncol = 7,
  guides = "collect"
) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "OV-bereikbaarheid van grootschalige woningbouwlocaties",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        family = if (use_atlas_grotesk) "Atlas Grotesk Medium" else NULL,
        size = 20)
    )
  ) &
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) &
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggsave(
  filename = "output/ptal_small_multiples_8km.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 16,
  height = 10,
  units = "in",
)

p +
  plot_annotation(title = NULL)
```

It immediately jumps out that several locations
have particularly poor public transport accessibility.
The largest are in:

* Flevoland (Almere, Zeewolde, and Lelystad)
* Haarlemmermeer
* Utrecht Rijnenburg
* Amersfoort A1 Zone

### Housing density

Of course, it may still be worthwhile to build housing
in public-transport poor areas if either:

1. new public transport links are planned, or
2. the proposed housing is low-density.

Or, put another way,
we could tailor the housing density across multiple locations
to build higher density in areas with high PTAL
and low density in public transport-poor areas,
while still achieving the same overall target number of units.

Let's take a location-by-location look.

```{r}
#| label: interactive-data-prep
#| include: false

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GWL choices and bounding boxes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

gwl_choices <- gwl |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(GWL) |>
  arrange(GWL) |>
  pull(GWL) |>
  as.character()

default_gwl <- if ("Alkmaar" %in% gwl_choices) {
  "Alkmaar"
} else {
  gwl_choices[[1]]
}

gwl_bounds <- gwl_wgs84 |>
  nest(.by = GWL) |>
  mutate(
    bbox = purrr::map(data, st_bbox),
    xmin = purrr::map_dbl(bbox, \(x) x[["xmin"]]),
    ymin = purrr::map_dbl(bbox, \(x) x[["ymin"]]),
    xmax = purrr::map_dbl(bbox, \(x) x[["xmax"]]),
    ymax = purrr::map_dbl(bbox, \(x) x[["ymax"]])
  ) |>
  select(GWL, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bevolking data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

gwl_bevolking <- gwl |>
  st_join(bevolking_pc6 |> select(aantal_woningen)) |>
  group_by(GWL) |>
  summarise(
    naam = first(GWL),
    bestaande_woningen = sum(aantal_woningen, na.rm = T),
    nieuwe_woningen_2030 = first(TOT2030),
    totaal_verwachte_woningen_2030 = bestaande_woningen + nieuwe_woningen_2030,
  ) |>
  mutate(
    area_ha = as.numeric(st_area(geom)) / 10000,
    dichtheid_bestaande_wo_per_ha = bestaande_woningen / area_ha,
    dichtheid_na_opbouwen_wo_per_ha = totaal_verwachte_woningen_2030 / area_ha
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aantal woningen
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

woning_data <- gwl_bevolking |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(
    GWL,
    bestaande_woningen,
    nieuwe_woningen_2030,
    totaal_verwachte_woningen_2030
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -GWL,
    names_to = "type",
    values_to = "woningen"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    GWL = as.character(GWL),
    type = recode(
      type,
      bestaande_woningen = "Bestaande woningen",
      nieuwe_woningen_2030 = "Nieuwe woningen",
      totaal_verwachte_woningen_2030 = "Totaal in 2030"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(woningen))

woning_over_70k <- gwl_bevolking |>
  filter(totaal_verwachte_woningen_2030 > 70000) |>
  pull(GWL) |>
  as.character()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Woningdichtheid
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

dichtheid_data <- gwl_bevolking |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(
    GWL,
    dichtheid_bestaande_wo_per_ha,
    dichtheid_na_opbouwen_wo_per_ha
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -GWL,
    names_to = "type",
    values_to = "dichtheid"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    GWL = as.character(GWL),
    type = recode(
      type,
      dichtheid_bestaande_wo_per_ha = "Bestaande woningen",
      dichtheid_na_opbouwen_wo_per_ha = "Na opbouwen"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(dichtheid))

dichtheid_over_200 <- gwl_bevolking |>
  filter(dichtheid_na_opbouwen_wo_per_ha > 200) |>
  pull(GWL) |>
  as.character()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pass data from R to Observable JS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ojs_define(
  gwl_choices_ojs = gwl_choices,
  default_gwl_ojs = default_gwl,
  gwl_bounds_ojs = gwl_bounds,
  woning_data_ojs = woning_data,
  woning_over_70k_ojs = woning_over_70k,
  dichtheid_data_ojs = dichtheid_data,
  dichtheid_over_200_ojs = dichtheid_over_200
)
```

    label: "Locatie:",

  }
)

    weight = 1,
    popup = ~ paste0(
      "<strong>", GWL, "</strong>", ": ", Subproject, "<br>",
      "CBS stedelijkheid (gemeente): ", stedelijkheid_gemeente, "<br>",
      "Woningen subproject: ", Subcapacit, "<br>",
      "Woningen project: ", Projcapaci, "<br>",
      "Woningen ", GWL, " 2030: ", TOT2030, "<br>",
      "Woningen ", GWL, " 2040: ", TOT2040, "<br>"
    )
  ) |>
  addPolygons(
    data = gwl_wgs84,
    fill = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 0.5
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = ptal_pal(ptal_levels),
    labels = ptal_levels,
    title = "PTAL"
  ) |>
  addScaleBar(
    position = "bottomleft",
    options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)
  ) |>
  fitBounds(
    default_bbox$xmin,
    default_bbox$ymin,
    default_bbox$xmax,
    default_bbox$ymax,
    options = list(maxZoom = 13, padding = c(10, 10))
  ) |>
  htmlwidgets::onRender("
    function(el, x) {
      const map = this;

      document.addEventListener('gwl-location-change', function(event) {
        map.fitBounds(event.detail, {
          maxZoom: 13,
          padding: [30, 30]
        });
      });
    }
  ")

## Cycling

In this analysis, we seek to develop
a meaningful measure of the **bicycle accessibility**
of the grootschalige woningbouwlocaties.
This is a difficult task because of their large-scale nature—as
these locations are often whole new urban districts
with associated new street infrastructure, amenities, and even jobs,
assessments of existing cycling infrastructure give an incomplete picture.

Therefore, we choose to focus our analysis on **job accessibility**,
as employment opportunities and locations are less likely to change
with the development of new housing,
when compared with street infrastructure itself
or amenities within neighborhoods.

As a rudimentary approach,
we can consider the number of jobs
available within cycling distance of the new housing areas
and make comparisons between them.

A more advanced analysis
could distribute hypothetical new citizens across these housing areas
and calculate job accessibility metrics for them on an individual basis.

### Existing jobs within cycling distance

City planners
[typically use](https://www.mrdh.nl/interview/potentie-fiets-woon-werkverkeer)
7,5 km as the maximum distance cycled to work in the Netherlands,
with 15 km for e-bikes.
We can therefore take a 7,5 km buffer around the large-scale housing areas
as a very rough estimate of the bike-accessible employment area.[^fiets-1]

[^fiets-1]: The actual area is smaller,
because it would reflect network distance rather than crow-flies distance
and account for the fact that not all residents live on the edge of the area.

We then count the number of jobs available in these employment areas
and normalize by the expected number of new households in 2030.

```{r}
#| label: calc-basic-buffer
#| cache: true

# constants
dist_bike <- 7.5 # bike distance in km
dist_ebike <- 15 # ebike distance in km

# buffer housing areas
gwl_bike_buffer  <- st_buffer(gwl, dist =  dist_bike * 1000)
gwl_ebike_buffer <- st_buffer(gwl, dist = dist_ebike * 1000)

# jobs per new resident

jobs <- gwl_bike_buffer |>
  select(oid, ProjNAAM, TOT2030) |>
  # first, join jobs data
  st_join(lisa |> select("BANEN")) |>
  group_by(oid) |>
  summarise(
    ProjNAAM = first(ProjNAAM),
    TOT2030 = first(TOT2030),
    banen = sum(BANEN, na.rm = T)
  ) |>
  # then, join households data
  st_join(bevolking_pc6 |> select(aantal_woningen)) |>
  group_by(oid) |>
  summarise(
    ProjNAAM = first(ProjNAAM),
    nieuwe_woningen_2030 = first(TOT2030),
    banen = first(banen),
    bestaande_woningen = sum(aantal_woningen, na.rm = T),
    banen_per_nieuwe_woning = banen / nieuwe_woningen_2030,
    banen_per_totaal_woningen = banen / (bestaande_woningen + nieuwe_woningen_2030)
  )
```

Then, we can plot these.

```{r}
#| label: map-jobs-cycling-distance

jobs_long <- jobs |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      banen,
      banen_per_nieuwe_woning,
      banen_per_totaal_woningen
    ),
    names_to = "group",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  arrange(group, value)

labels <- c(
  banen = "Banen",
  banen_per_nieuwe_woning = "Banen per nieuwe\nwoning (2030)",
  banen_per_totaal_woningen = "Banen per totaal aantal woningen\n(inclusief bestaande en gepland)"
)

palettes <- c(
  banen = "viridis",
  banen_per_nieuwe_woning = "cividis",
  banen_per_totaal_woningen = "inferno"
)

make_job_map <- function(data) {
  group <- unique(data$group)

  ggplot(data) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = value), color = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_sf(data = nl_border, fill = NA) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = palettes[[group]],
      labels = scales::label_number()
    ) +
    labs(fill = labels[[group]]) +
    theme_void()
}

plots <- jobs_long |>
  group_split(group) |>
  map(make_job_map)
```
